> **Draft:** the docs and config are complete and pass all local checks. On-hardware verification on Atlas 800I A3 is pending (see Accuracy Tests below).

## Motivation

Refs Ascend/sglang#1211.

The GLM-5.2 cookbook has no Ascend NPU option, although the [Ascend NPU GLM-5.2 tutorial](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/glm_5_2) documents a single-node PD mixed recipe and a 1P1D PD disaggregation recipe. This PR adds both to the deploy panel, so you can pick **Atlas 800I A3** and get a command for each scenario.

## Modifications

### Commit 1: GLM-5.2 A3 data (`glm-5.2.jsx`, `GLM-5.2.mdx`)

| Deploy selection | Scenario | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| A3 · W8A8 · Balanced · Single Node | 1×A3 PD Mixed (16 dies) | `--tp-size 16`, DeepEP auto, NEXTN 3-1-4 |
| A3 · W8A8 · High-Throughput · **PD Prefill (2 nodes)** | 2×A3 1P1D, prefill node | `--tp-size 16 --dp-size 4`, DeepEP normal, graph capture off, NEXTN 1-1-2 |
| A3 · W8A8 · High-Throughput · **PD Decode (2 nodes)** | 2×A3 1P1D, decode node | `--tp-size 16 --dp-size 16 --ep-size 16`, DeepEP low_latency, NEXTN 3-1-4 |

- Checkpoint: `Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w8a8` (msModelSlim W8A8, 774 GB; `--quantization modelslim`). The W8A8 chip appears only on A3. The checkpoint's MTP layer (layer 78) is stored as FLOAT per its `quant_model_description.json`, so every recipe passes `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant`.
- The PD roles sit in the **Nodes** row because each role is its own server started with `--nnodes 1`, so they don't fit a `multi-2` cell. The router command is in the page text.
- The recipes are transcribed from the tutorial. Flags the tutorial scripts use that `main` has deprecated are replaced with their current spellings: `--cuda-graph-bs` → `--cuda-graph-bs-decode`, `--cuda-graph-max-bs` → `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`, `--disable-cuda-graph` → `--cuda-graph-backend-{decode,prefill} disabled`, `--moe-dense-tp` → `--moe-dense-tp-size`. `--prefill-round-robin-balance` is dropped because it is a no-op `DeprecatedAction` on `main`.
- `dockerImages.a3` is set to `quay.io/ascend/sglang:cann9.0.0-a3-v0.5.16` (the tutorial's image). The PD roles use host networking, and the config adds `NETWORK_IFACE` / `PREFILL_IP` placeholders for `HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` and `ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL`.
- On A3, the Playground hides the cards that would emit CUDA-only flags (Attention, PD Disagg, HiCache, and the MoE EP degrees) and greys out the EAGLE presets with a reason: the NPU path is NEXTN.
- Page: the install section notes the CANN image, and Configuration Tips gains an Ascend section with a topology table, weights, host preparation, cross-node networking, the router command, and the verification status.
- All three cells are marked `verificationStatus: "in-progress"`, the same as the Kimi-K3 A3 cell in #35508.

### Commit 2: Playground fix (`_playground.jsx`, `authoring-reference.md`)

The A3 PD Prefill / PD Decode cells carry their own `--disaggregation-*` flags. The PD Disagg card is hidden on A3, but `applyAllDeltas` still ran its `apply`, which clears the `--disaggregation-*` family and then re-adds the role picked on the card. On A3 the card's role stays "off", so **the Playground command silently lost `--disaggregation-mode`** and turned the role recipe into a PD mixed one. The Deploy panel was not affected.

The fix skips an axis whose axis-level `showWhen(base)` hides its card, using the same predicate the renderer uses. There is one line of logic; the rest is comments and the documentation sync that `engine-axis.md` §3.4 asks for.

**No existing page changes behavior.** I scanned all 14 configs on `main` that declare a PD card. The bug only triggers when base cells carry `--disaggregation-*` flags *and* the card owns the role, and only GLM-5.2 meets both conditions: Kimi-K3 has PD cells but no card-owned role, and the other 12 configs have no PD cells.

## Accuracy Tests

Pending. The on-hardware runs need 2× Atlas 800I A3 **full nodes** (16 dies each). The HiDevLab environment available to me is 1 card / 2 dies, so I've asked for resources in Ascend/sglang#1211. Once the runs are done, the numbers will go into `glm-5.2-benchmarks.jsx` and the cells will be flipped to verified.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Pending, same as above.

## Verification done without hardware

- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs`: OK
- `mint validate` and `mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` (mint 4.2.559, same as CI): both pass on this branch
- CPU dry-run through `sglang.srt.server_args.prepare_server_args()`, the `sglang serve` entry point: all three generated commands parse and resolve on this branch with exit 0 and no warnings.
- All 52 existing GPU cells are byte-identical to `main`.
- Browser walk-through with `mint dev` and Playwright (on an earlier base): A3 selection snaps to W8A8, strategy and nodes gating work, the Python and Docker commands match the cells, and after commit 2 the Playground keeps the PD flags.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit (codespell, whitespace; `glm-5.2.jsx` keeps its CRLF line endings).
- [ ] Add unit tests — N/A (docs/config only; covered by `check_cookbook_configs.mjs`).
- [x] Update documentation.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — pending hardware (see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

+description: "Deploy GLM-5.2 with SGLang — Z.ai's DeepSeek-Sparse-Attention (DSA) Mixture-of-Experts model with MTP speculative decoding and 1M context, on H200, B200, B300, GB300, AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X, and Ascend Atlas 800I A3 NPUs."
 ---
 
 ## Deployment
@@ -37,6 +37,10 @@ For how to launch the image, see [Install → Method 3: Using Docker](../../../d
 
 </Tabs>
 
+<Note>
+  **Ascend NPU (Atlas 800I A3).** Use the CANN image `quay.io/ascend/sglang:cann9.0.0-a3-v0.5.16` instead of `lmsysorg/sglang` — pick **Atlas 800I A3** below and the Docker tab emits the full `docker run`, including the 16 `davinci` devices and the host driver/firmware mounts. To build from source instead, see [SGLang installation with NPU support](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation).
+</Note>
+
 </Accordion>
 
 Pick your hardware + recipe to generate the launch command. The three serving strategies cover the common operating points:
@@ -126,6 +130,42 @@ import { Playground } from "/src/snippets/_playground.jsx";
 
 - **MTP / EAGLE speculative decoding on AMD.** Five-step MTP is validated for `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` on MI355X with `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260910`. Choose **Low-Latency** for the GPU-resident TP8/EP1 topology, or **High-Throughput** for the TP4/EP4 topology. Both emit `--speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6` with the Triton DSA prefill and decode backends. The TP4/EP4 InferenceX benchmark adds HiCache DRAM offload, but those host-specific knobs are intentionally omitted from the portable cookbook command. MTP remains unvalidated for GLM-5.2 on MI300X/MI325X and for the other MI355X checkpoint precisions.
 
+<a id="ascend-npu-atlas-800i-a3" />
+
+**Ascend NPU (Atlas 800I A3).** One A3 node is 8 cards × 2 dies = **16 devices**, so every A3 recipe runs `--tp-size 16` per node. Pick **W8A8**, then use the **Nodes** row to choose the topology:
+
+| Nodes | Hardware | What it starts |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Single Node** | 1 × A3 (16 dies) | one PD mixed server that prefills and decodes |
+| **PD Prefill** + **PD Decode** | 2 × A3 (32 dies) | one server per role (1P1D), fronted by a router |
+
+- **Weights.** The A3 recipes use the msModelSlim INT8 build [`Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w8a8`](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w8a8/) (774 GB), which fits one node's 16 × 64 GB. The cells set `SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE=1` so `--model-path` resolves against ModelScope; point it at a local directory instead once the weights are downloaded, and put that directory on shared storage for a two-node deployment. Quantization covers the main model only — the MTP (nextn) layer stays BF16, which is why every recipe passes `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant`. The BF16 checkpoint (`zai-org/GLM-5.2`, ~1.5 TB) needs two nodes and is not covered by the NPU recipes here.
+- **Prepare the host.** Put the CPUs in performance mode and keep the NUMA balancer out of the way before you start the server; the Ascend recipes assume it:
+
+  ```bash Command
+  echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
+  sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
+  sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
+  sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
+  ```
+
+  Inside the container, source CANN first: `source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh` and `source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh`.
+- **Wire up the two nodes (PD only).** Set `HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` and `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` to the interface that carries each node's own IP (`ifconfig`), and give both roles the **same** `ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL`, pointing at the prefill node — it is the rendezvous for the KV transfer. Start the prefill role first, then the decode role.
+- **Front the roles with a router (PD only).** Start it once both roles are up, and match the ports to what the Deploy panel emits (`--port`, plus the prefill role's `--disaggregation-bootstrap-port`):
+
+  ```bash Command
+  python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \
+      --pd-disaggregation \
+      --policy round_robin \
+      --prefill http://<prefill-node-ip>:30000 8998 \
+      --decode http://<decode-node-ip>:30000 \
+      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  Send requests to the router's port, not to either role.
+- **NPU-specific knobs stay out of the Playground.** The Attention, PD Disagg and Hierarchical KV Cache cards are hidden on A3 and the EAGLE presets are greyed out: NPU prefill context parallelism uses `--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel` / `--nsa-prefill-cp-mode`, the NPU MTP path is `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN`, and the two PD roles are full recipes in the Deploy panel rather than a toggle on top of the PD mixed one.
+- **These recipes are still being verified.** They are transcribed from the [Ascend NPU GLM-5.2 tutorial](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/glm_5_2) and marked **In progress** until they are verified on Atlas 800I A3 hardware, so the benchmark card carries no NPU numbers yet. For NPU tuning, accuracy and profiling, see [parameter tuning](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/optimization/parameter_tuning), [accuracy evaluation](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/evaluation/accuracy_evaluation) and [performance testing](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/evaluation/performance_testing); for anything that fails to start, the [Ascend NPU FAQ](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/faq).
+
 ## 3. Advanced Usage
 
 ### 3.1 Reasoning

     { id: "high-throughput", label: "High-Throughput" },
   ],

-    { id: "single",  label: "Single Node" },
-    { id: "multi-2", label: "Multi-Nodes" },

+      disabled: (s) => s.hw === "a3" && s.strategy !== "balanced",

+    { id: "multi-2", label: "Multi-Nodes",

+      disableReason: "On Atlas 800I A3, PD disaggregation is the High-Throughput recipe — switch Strategy to High-Throughput first." },
+    { id: "pd-decode",  label: "PD Decode (2 nodes)",
+      showWhen: (s) => s.hw === "a3",
+      disabled: (s) => s.strategy !== "high-throughput",
+      disableReason: "On Atlas 800I A3, PD disaggregation is the High-Throughput recipe — switch Strategy to High-Throughput first." },
   ],
 
   modelNames: {
     "default|fp8": "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8",
     "default|bf16": "zai-org/GLM-5.2",
     "default|nvfp4": "nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4",
     "default|mxfp4": "amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4",
+    // ModelScope repo — pair with SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE=1 (set in the A3 cells).
+    "default|w8a8": "Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w8a8",
   },
 
   placeholders: {
     HOST_IP:   { target: "command", label: "Bind host",         default: "0.0.0.0"  },
     PORT:      { target: "command", label: "Bind port",         default: "30000"    },
     NODE0_IP:  { target: "command", label: "Head node IP",      default: "<node0-ip>"   },
     NODE_RANK: { target: "command", label: "This node rank",    default: "<node-rank>"  },
+    NETWORK_IFACE: { target: "command", label: "Cross-node NIC",  default: "<your-nic>"       },
+    PREFILL_IP:    { target: "command", label: "Prefill node IP", default: "<prefill-node-ip>" },
     CURL_HOST: { target: "curl",    label: "Server host",       default: "localhost" },
     CURL_PORT: { target: "curl",    label: "Server port",       default: "30000"     },
   },
@@ -100,8 +129,16 @@ sgl-eval run aime25 \\
     "mi355x|mxfp4": "lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260910",
     mi325x: "lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.13.post1-rocm700-mi30x-20260616",
     mi300x: "lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.13.post1-rocm700-mi30x-20260616",
+    // CANN 9.0.0 release image for Atlas 800I A3 (daily builds are tagged
+    // main-cann9.0.0-a3). See the Ascend NPU quickstart for the A2 image.
+    a3: "quay.io/ascend/sglang:cann9.0.0-a3-v0.5.16",
   },
 
+  // Each PD role launches with --nnodes 1, so the multi-node branch does not
